_readme: Reasoning-effort ladders, per model, as reported by the OpenRouter catalog's
`reasoning` block. Copied here so a pinned effort is auditable and so pre-flight
can refuse an effort a model does not list.
Why this exists: effort is a confound on the order of temperature. The same model
at "low" and at "max" is a different experiment. The levels are model specific -
there is no universal ladder - and an UNLISTED level is often silently rendered as
the provider's default, which would misdescribe the run. So the runner refuses a
level the model does not list rather than sending it.
`mandatory: true` means reasoning cannot be switched off for that model; the
lowest rung is as close to "off" as it gets. An empty `supportedEfforts` means the
model lists no rungs at all (the parameter is omitted and the provider default
applies) - it is NOT the same as ["none"], which is an explicit level.
Absent model = unknown ladder. Pre-flight then refuses a pinned effort (it cannot
prove the level is accepted) but still permits an unset effort.
Re-derive a row: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, the model's `reasoning`
